Thanks — good set of questions. Below is our standard operating approach for on-prem/offline evidence handling; happy to iterate for FinHealth specifics.

Summary (high level)
- Media: We support encrypted, HSM-signed USB images and sealed encrypted NVMe devices for updates and evidence transport. We do not accept raw unencrypted media.
- Chain-of-custody: Manifest signed by Redwood Logistics Ops + customer representative at handoff. Manifest fields: sender/recipient, device serial, checksum (sha256), tamper seal ID, time of transfer, courier name and license.
- Carrier: We use bonded couriers for high-value transfers; insurance up to insured value on PO. Alternative: local courier approved by customer with pre-shared manifest.
- Maintenance windows: Standard weekly windows are Tue/Wed 01:00-04:00 UTC. For emergencies we support out-of-window maintenance with advance notice and an expedited fee.
- Support SLA: For on-prem Private customers with the Dedicated+Compliance package: 4 hr response for Sev1 (business hours), 8 hr for after-hours; remediation TTR varies by hardware access.
- Customer requirements: Onsite witness + signed manifest at exchange OR PoA (power of attorney) delegation form. Background checks for 3rd party personnel can be accommodated on request.

Operational steps (detailed)
1) Pre-transfer: Redwood provides a transfer request packet (includes PO number, insured value, manifest template).
2) Image prep: Build image in isolated build farm, sign with our HSM key, produce signed manifest and sha256 checksums.
3) Packaging: Tamper-evident bag, seal ID recorded on manifest.
4) Handoff: Bonded courier picks up at Redwood logistics facility; courier signs outbound manifest.
5) Delivery: Customer or approved onsite witness signs incoming manifest; customer sends photo of seal + manifest to sig-evidence@redwood.ai.
6) Verification: On acceptance, customer confirms sha256 and seals intact. If verification fails, device quarantined and incident opened.
